title: Ripple posterior export
description: Everything the browser needs to simulate scenarios without a server. Written by model/ripple_model/export.py, read by web/lib/simulate.ts. Array shapes use D=n_draws, C=n_cities, S=n_segments, P=n_traits, K=2*n_fourier, W=n_history_rows.

cities.description: Training city names, index order = C.

segments.description: Segment names, index order = S. ['All'] when the CSV has no segment column.

weeks.description: Number of distinct training weeks. Future week index t starts at this value.

n_draws.description: D — posterior draws kept in this export.

base_price.description: Reference price in the log-log elasticity term.

unit_cost.description: Default variable cost per unit; a scenario may override it.

shares.description: shares[c][s] — segment share of city c, rows sum to 1. Enters log mu as the offset log(share).

trait_names.description: P city-trait names, e.g. ['log_population','median_income_k','share_age_18_34']. Empty when has_traits is false.

trait_mean.description: Training mean per trait, raw units — used to standardize a new city.

trait_std.description: Training sd per trait, raw units.

trait_min.description: Minimum of each STANDARDIZED trait across training cities. A new city outside [min,max] raises the extrapolation flag.

trait_max.description: Maximum of each STANDARDIZED trait across training cities.

has_promo.description: False when the CSV had no promo column: b_promo and b_dip are all zeros and promo scenarios are disabled.

has_feature.description: False when the CSV had no feature column: b_feature is all zeros.

has_traits.description: False disables new-city scenarios; the UI must say why.

has_segments.description: False means a single pseudo-segment 'All'; the UI hides segment bars.

season_period.description: Weeks per seasonal cycle, 52 for weekly data.

n_fourier.description: Number of Fourier PAIRS. The season design row for week t is [sin(2*pi*1*t/period), cos(2*pi*1*t/period), ..., sin(2*pi*n*t/period), cos(2*pi*n*t/period)], length K = 2*n_fourier.

method.description: Sampler and settings actually used, e.g. 'nutpie NUTS, 4 chains x 1000 draws' or 'Pathfinder (fast approximation)'.

fast_approximation.description: True when the fit fell back to Pathfinder/ADVI under the BYOD time limit; the UI labels the run.

draws.description: Posterior draws, draw index first. Terms that do not apply are present and filled with zeros, so the simulator never branches on missing keys.

g.description: [D][P] trait coefficients: a_city_hat = g0 + X_z . g.

tau_city.description: [D] sd of the city effect around its trait prediction; the new-city uncertainty.

e.description: [D][S] price elasticity per segment, multiplies log(price/base_price). Negative means demand falls when price rises.

b_promo.description: [D][S] deal-signal lift per segment, multiplies the 0/1 promo flag.

b_feature.description: [D] lift of the feature flag (shared across segments).

b_dip.description: [D] post-promo pull-forward effect, multiplies promo_last_week. Expected to be negative.

phi.description: [D] Negative Binomial dispersion; var = mu + mu^2/phi.

history.description: Observed training rows in columnar form (smaller JSON than row objects). All arrays have the same length W.

week_start.description: ISO date of the Monday of each row's week.

candidates.description: Cities the user can launch in. Empty when has_traits is false.

shares.description: [S] expected segment mix of the new city.

extrapolation.description: True when any standardized trait is outside [trait_min, trait_max].

out_of_range_traits.description: Names of the traits that are out of range; drives the UI banner text.
